Last week, after the release of Xcode 27.1 beta 1, Bitrig immediately added support for building and testing iPhone Duo apps, along with an interactive 3D simulator that lets developers freely fold, tilt, rotate and position the device. Details below.

Bitrig now lets users experience a 3D iPhone Duo

Bitrig originally launched as a simple vibe-coding application, where users can generate native SwiftUI apps directly within the Bitrig main app on iPhone via text or voice commands.

Since then, it has expanded significantly, adding a Mac app that gives users access to the full Xcode toolchain, an integrated iPhone simulator, on-device testing, and the ability to export projects to Xcode or publish apps via TestFlight and the App Store.

Last Friday, after Apple released Xcode 27.1 beta 1 supporting the build and testing of iPhone Duo apps, Bitrig quickly rolled out its own iPhone Duo support, reinterpreting the simulator in a more interactive way.

Below, Bitrig co-founder and CEO Kyle Macomber walks through what this update has to offer:

Experiment with different postures. The iPhone Duo can lie flat on a table like a laptop, or stand on a bedside table like a tent. Whether fully open, fully closed, or half-folded, in portrait or landscape, your apps must adapt flexibly. Bitrig's 3D simulator lets you pick it up, fold it and rotate it on the fly, observing how your app responds in real time. Respond to hinge state. Use onHingeChange to detect when the phone opens and closes, driving interactions and effects that mimic Apple's unfolding animations, making the outer screen feel like a window into the inner screen. Read hinge data live during the opening and closing process in the built-in simulator. Build hands-free experiences. Use ArrangementView to place media content in the top half and controls in the bottom half, making it easy to use when the iPhone Duo is lying flat on a table. Support landscape orientation so users can operate your app via the outer screen when the device is standing on its side. Use both screens at once. Add CameraCaptureAccessory to the outer screen to provide useful information for users facing the camera.

Macomber also added: "Bitrig helps you manage multiple versions of Xcode, so you can start preparing your apps for iPhone Duo with the beta, then switch back to Xcode 27 anytime to continue building and releasing updates."

For more information about Bitrig's latest update and how to use its iPhone Duo simulator, click here.
